_comment: The composed visual identity for this slot, read by scripts/store-studio.py. Everything the studio draws - the launcher icon, the adaptive-icon vectors in app/src/main/res/drawable, the feature graphic and the screenshot compositions - is derived from `mark` and `palette` here, so this file is the one place the store presence is decided. It is not optional: the studio refuses to render without it, because falling back to the generic renderer changes the whole pack while store/graphics.md keeps describing the composed one. The palette below is the same palette as app/src/main/java/com/gexetr/lawnroundlog/ui/theme/Color.kt, value for value - two sources for one colour is how a pack ends up describing a different app than the one the user installs.
_mark: `mark-stripes` is the mown-stripe fan: four bold stripes converging toward a vanishing point above them, the pattern a mower leaves on a lawn, with the two inner stripes in the cut accent and the two outer in chalk. It says mowing, it says a row, and it says 'just cut' - and it is not a page, a check, a caliper or any other slot's glyph. Geometry, in the canonical fractions scripts/lib/icon_design.py speaks (canvas = the 108dp adaptive viewport), so registering it in `MARK_REGISTRY` is mechanical: four `stroke` primitives at the declared `bold` weight (24px/512 = 0.046875), round caps, each a two-point line from top to bottom. topY = 0.350, bottomY = 0.650. (topX, bottomX, role): (0.385, 0.315, 'paper'), (0.462, 0.438, 'amber'), (0.538, 0.562, 'amber'), (0.615, 0.685, 'paper'). Measured against the grid: silhouette bbox x=[0.2916, 0.7084] y=[0.3266, 0.6734], centre exactly (0.5, 0.5) = the optical anchor; extent 0.4169 (limit 0.6667 visible); reach 0.2616 = 28.25dp = 91% of the 31.00dp circle keyline (floor 75%); ink coverage of the 66dp safe zone ~0.17 (window 0.15-0.85; measured 0.1738 of the safe square, analytic 0.1714 — the earlier ~0.24 was wrong, corrected 2026-10-02); mark outside the safe circle 0px; thinnest stroke 24px and 2.25px at 48dp (floor 16px / 1.5px).
_palette: One deliberate identity, shared with the app's own theme (app/src/main/java/com/gexetr/lawnroundlog/ui/theme/Color.kt): a mown-lawn field of deep turf green, chalk-off-white for ink and display text, and one lime reserved for work that has just been done. Roles the studio draws with: `ink`/`ink_soft`/`ink_lift` are the three ends of the background gradient, `amber` is the cut accent on the stripes and the pill outline, `amber_deep` and `amber_pale` are its darker and lighter accents, `accent_deep` is the cool chalk-slate glow that gives the field depth, `paper` is the chalk mark and the display text, `muted` is secondary text, and `bezel`/`bezel_rim` are the device mock-up frame.
_claim_bounds: Every headline must be true of the shipped build. The app keeps an ordered round of customers, records mowed/skipped/rained-off visits, pushes the round by one day, derives a running balance per customer from billable visits minus payments, exports CSV through the system file picker, and works with no account and no network in the daily path. It does not sync, does not share anything with anyone, does not schedule appointments and cannot promise a customer will pay. So 'Never lose a customer' is a guarantee the app cannot make and 'Syncs with your office' is false. Each headline below names something the app verifiably does, and the shot behind it is asserted by store/journey.json.
_headlines: One headline per journey shot, in journey order, kept to 3-5 words so it stays readable at thumbnail size. The studio falls back to the shot title when this list is short, so a short list would silently change the pack. The order tracks the journey: the ordered round, a recorded visit, a pushed morning, the money owed, the export, and the shelf claim.
featureTagline: An offline round log for a one-man mowing round. No account, no ads, bought once.
